text: Abel's blood cried out for vengeance. Jesus' blood "speaks better things": forgiveness, healing, restoration.
explanation:
The first time blood is mentioned in the Bible, God tells Cain, "The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground." Blood has a voice before God, and Abel's cried for justice against his murderer.

But you have come "to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than that of Abel." The world nailed God's Son to a cross, and God turned that very act into the means of forgiving the world. Right now His blood is speaking for you: forgiven, reconciled, healed, provided for. "See that you do not refuse Him who speaks."

text: Jesus closed the scroll mid-sentence, at "the acceptable year of the Lord," before "the day of vengeance." We live in that comma.
explanation:
In the Nazareth synagogue, Jesus read Isaiah 61: "to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord." Then He rolled up the scroll and sat down. In Isaiah the sentence carries straight on: "and the day of vengeance of our God." He stopped exactly where His first coming stops.

The day of vengeance is real, and it's coming, but it isn't now. For two thousand years, God has been proclaiming the year of His favour. Even when the world is shaken, don't read today's troubles as His wrath on you. Christ "delivers us from the wrath to come." This is still the season of grace.

text: God shakes what can be shaken "that the things which cannot be shaken may remain." You're receiving an unshakable kingdom.
explanation:
"Yet once more I shake not only the earth, but also heaven." This shaking removes "those things that are being shaken, as of things that are made": man-made things we quietly trusted instead of God, like financial systems, our own methods of raising children, even our confidence in medicine alone. Keep taking what your doctor prescribes, but don't put your trust in it.

In army training, the sergeant made you jump to see which camouflage fell off. What's fixed stays put. "Since we are receiving a kingdom which cannot be shaken," build your life on what God has built: His grace, His word, His ways. When everything else wobbles, you'll still be standing.

text: "Let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear." Reverence grows from grace, not dread.
explanation:
Many believe fear of punishment will make people holy. But can a child truly obey a father he's always afraid will cast him out? Hebrews says reverence comes through grace: "Let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably." And John says, "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves torment": the dread of punishment.

After 9/11, churches overflowed with frightened people; within months, they emptied again. Fear doesn't last. "The love of Christ compels us." When you know all wrath is behind you and only favour lies ahead, you become holy almost by accident.

text: The Passover lamb wasn't to be eaten raw or boiled, but "roasted in fire." Admiring Jesus' teaching isn't enough. Feed on His cross.
explanation:
"Do not eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted in fire." Many people respect Jesus as a great teacher and admire the Sermon on the Mount, yet aren't saved. That's eating Him raw. Others water down what happened at the cross. That's eating Him boiled.

Roasted in fire means seeing the Lamb under the fire of God's judgment, taking the punishment that was meant for you. That's where the nourishment is. "Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed for us." When you take Communion, don't just remember a good man. See Him bearing your sin, your sickness and your judgment, out of love for you.

text: Israel ate the lamb's head, legs and inwards, and walked out of Egypt with "none feeble among their tribes."
explanation:
God was specific: eat "its head with its legs and its entrails." Each part points to Jesus. The head: He knew no sin. The legs: He did no sin, but "went about doing good and healing all." The inwards: in Him is no sin. No wonder the Father opened heaven and said, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."

After eating that lamb, two to three million people, many of them elderly and worn out by slavery, walked out strong. "There was none feeble among His tribes." If the shadow did that, how much more the substance? Each time you take the Lord's Supper, receive His sound mind, His strong legs, His whole body for yours.

text: "If the household is too small for the lamb…" The Lamb is always bigger than your need.
explanation:
God never said, "If the lamb is too small for the household." It's always the household that's too small for the Lamb. Jesus came first to the lost sheep of Israel, but His sacrifice was far greater than one nation's need; it was for the whole world.

Whatever the size of your problem, your debt, your depression or your diagnosis, His supply exceeds it. His love is lavish love, enough to fill every empty place in your heart with plenty left over. Anointed preaching makes much of Jesus and nothing of the devil. Make Him big in your eyes today.
